artifacts.summary: 3-phase plan to land the two verified ModelExistence -> Compact bridge theorems into StrongCompleteness.lean, reconcile seven stale prose sites, and run the full acceptance gate.

memory_candidates.content: In the BimodalLogic FormalSystem tree, FormalSystem/Metalogic/SetConsequence.lean is deliberately vocabulary-only (Prop-valued statements of open obligations: StrongCompletenessBase, CompactBase, SatisfiableBaseSet, ModelExistenceBase and Dense siblings), while FormalSystem/Metalogic/StrongCompleteness.lean owns the foldr-implication bridge lemmas (truthAt_foldr_imp, derivable_foldr_imp_iff) and imports SetConsequence.lean. Consequence: any THEOREM about SetConsequence.lean's vocabulary whose proof consumes one of those bridge lemmas must live in StrongCompleteness.lean, not next to the definitions it is stated against -- placing it beside the definitions is an import cycle. This has now forced four theorems downstream (strongCompletenessBase_of_compact, strongCompletenessDense_of_compact, compactBase_of_modelExistence, compactDense_of_modelExistenceDense). A task brief that says 'prove X in SetConsequence.lean' should be read as 'in SetConsequence.lean or a sibling' and resolved to StrongCompleteness.lean whenever the proof route touches truthAt_foldr_imp. A side benefit preserved by this split: SetConsequence.lean's module-docstring claim that no compactness result is proved or refuted there stays literally true.
